Read an Element lazily

Source: R/lazy-read.R
read_elem_lazy.Rd

read_elem_lazy() reads the metadata of an Element and leaves its data on disk, so values are read only when they are realised or processed by block. It matches Python's read_elem_lazy().

Usage

read_elem_lazy(store, path = "/", chunks = NULL)

Arguments

store

An h5ad file or a zarr directory (v3 or v2), given as a path or as an open store handle.

path

Path of the Element within the store.

chunks

Chunk shape of the DelayedArray grid, one entry per dimension, where NA or -1 is the whole axis. The default is the on-disk chunking (1000 where an HDF5 array is contiguous) and for sparse arrays the major axis is cut every 1000 positions. Sparse arrays can only be chunked along the major axis. Ignored for string, categorical, nullable and dataframe Elements.

Value

A DelayedArray, or a lazy column or data frame.

Details

What is returned depends on the encoding of the Element:

  • dense and sparse (CSR and CSC) arrays are DelayedArrays, sparse ones stay sparse (SparseArray) when processed by block

  • string arrays are 1-d DelayedArrays of character

  • categorical and nullable arrays are lazy columns, and a dataframe is a lazy data frame whose columns are lazy

  • other encodings (such as dict and scalars) raise anndata_io_registry_error, as in Python

Realising a lazy value gives what read_h5ad() and read_zarr() give for the same Element, including NA and the On-disk dtype records. The store stays open while any lazy object that uses it exists.

Deviations from Python

store is a path or an open store handle, because R has no element object like h5py's. See vignette("deviations") for the full list.

Examples

adata <- AnnData(matrix(as.numeric(1:6), nrow = 3))
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".zarr")
write_zarr(adata, path)
read_elem_lazy(path, "X")
#> <3 x 2> DelayedMatrix object of type "double":
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    1    4
#> [2,]    2    5
#> [3,]    3    6
